key_insight: TIM separates disease-specific image features from temporal changes, then iteratively refines prior and current radiology reports to improve longitudinal consistency.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help radiologists document changes across examinations, but clinical benefit and safety remain unestablished.
method: Decouple spatial pathology features from temporal evolution patterns.
Generate reports for both prior and current studies.
Use error-sensitive mutual feedback to iteratively refine both reports.
evidence_signal: On Longitudinal-MIMIC, TIM reportedly outperformed single-image and longitudinal baselines across language and clinical metrics; the abstract provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Revising prior reports requires safeguards to preserve the original clinical record and prevent incorrect retrospective changes.
paper_title: TIM: Temporal Decoupling with Iterative Mutual-Refinement Model for Longitudinal Radiology Report Generation
